hlni.insight: Business Organization & Management appears in Semester I of both JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents (2025-26 cohort).
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree names imply absolute separation of curriculum.
hlni.viewerChange: Viewer moves from binary degree choice to module-level curriculum investigation.
hlni.support: Verifiable via official documents: B.Com Accounting & Finance p.5 and BBA Entrepreneurship Management p.9.
hlni.payoff: The student stops guessing and starts mapping full curricula, demonstrating a more grounded research method.

candidate.reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: The Shared Subject Myth
candidate.creativeAngle: Evidence-based curriculum comparison to debunk degree-title assumptions.
candidate.objective: Guide students to research actual curriculum depth rather than relying on degree labels.
candidate.targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Binary Choice
shots.visual: A student holds two brochures, B.Com and BBA, looking confused.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA feels like picking completely different worlds.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on student face, transitioning to the brochures.

shots.name: The Title Trap
shots.visual: Student taps the titles of the brochures, looking skeptical.
shots.dialogue: We assume the names tell us everything about the content.
shots.cameraPerformance: Tight shot on hands tapping brochure covers.

shots.name: Document Reveal
shots.visual: Student opens both official PDFs on a laptop screen side-by-side.
shots.dialogue: But look at the actual programme documents.
shots.cameraPerformance: Camera pans from student to the laptop screen.

shots.name: The Shared Module
shots.visual: Highlighting Semester I in both documents.
shots.dialogue: Both list Business Organization & Management. The labels hide the overlap.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on laptop screen showing the matching rows.

shots.name: New Research Question
shots.visual: Student closes the laptop and writes a note in a journal.
shots.dialogue: So, what does the full curriculum reveal beyond this shared title?
shots.onscreenText: What does the full curriculum reveal beyond this shared title?

shots.name: Actionable Step
shots.visual: Student begins mapping modules from the PDFs into a comparison table.
shots.dialogue: Map the full modules to see the real difference.

productionNotes.camera: Stable, clear focus on document text.
productionNotes.editing: Direct cuts between shots to maintain focus.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use official programme documents to show that degree titles can mask shared core subjects, prompting better research.

storySpine.startingBelief: B.Com and BBA are entirely different worlds with no shared subjects.
storySpine.studentSituation: A +2 student is choosing between B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management.
storySpine.observation: Both programme documents list Business Organization & Management in Semester I.
storySpine.focus: The assumption that degree titles act as perfect barriers to shared core knowledge.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: If core subjects overlap, the choice must be based on more than just the degree name.
storySpine.changedAction: The student replaces a binary 'Which degree is better?' with 'What does the full curriculum reveal about specific learning depth?'
storySpine.visibleConsequence: The student shifts from guessing to mapping actual modules for both programmes.
storySpine.channelExperience: A direct reveal of course documents that breaks the student's binary choice habit.

selected.title: B.Com vs BBA: The Shared Subject Myth
selected.audienceGap: Students assume degree names imply absolute separation of content.
selected.hlni: Business Organization & Management is listed in Semester I of the published JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents whose covers say students admitted from 2025–26 onwards.
selected.viewerChange: Viewer stops relying on labels and starts looking for curriculum-based evidence.
selected.concept: Bounded curriculum comparison using official JOY University documents.
selected.support: Official JOY University PDF, B.Com Accounting & Finance p.5 and BBA Entrepreneurship Management p.9; covers identify the 2025–26-onwards cohort.
methodSteps: Identify the specific programme and document cohort.
Show the inspected course-title row in each source.
Use this bounded overlap to investigate the full course, rather than assume degree titles partition subjects.
selected.interpretationRule: The supplied rows establish this shared title in these two documents only; they do not establish identical teaching, depth, assessment or availability.
selected.visibleProof: Two real cited rows correct a title-based assumption while retaining programme/version scope.
selected.payoff: A more grounded method for researching course content.
selected.limitations: No universal overlap, identical content, exclusivity, current-admissions or career inference. BBA later sections are inconsistent; use only the inspected row.

demonstration.input: Two PDF document covers and internal Semester I course lists.
demonstration.observation: The same subject appears in both B.Com and BBA Semester I lists.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What does the full curriculum reveal beyond this shared title?

conceptSelection.contrast: Only Trust was planned and reviewed. Finished-story channel comparison is separate; this is not editorial approval.
